title: Prajāpate na tvad: none but you encompasses all that is born
theme: Prajāpati is told that no one but he encompasses all created things; the worshippers ask that what they desire in offering to him be theirs, and that they become lords of riches.

words.context: The anonymous commentator addresses him: «हे प्रजापते ब्रह्मन्पार्वतीवल्लभ»

words.role: object of pari babhūva, with viśvā jātāni

words.gram: past pass. part. n. acc. pl.

words.role: separated from its verb (tmesis): pari … babhūva

words.gram: pron. n. acc. pl. (Vedic tā for tāni)

words.meaning: has been; with pari, has encompassed
words.context: The anonymous commentator: «परिपूर्वो भवतिस्तिरस्कारार्थः» — bhū with pari means to overpower

sandhi.type: final t voiced before a vowel; i before a vowel; visarga after a before a voiced consonant
sandhi.rule: tvat before e becomes tvad; etāni before a becomes etāny; anyaḥ before v becomes anyo.

sandhi.type: visarga before t; t before a nasal
sandhi.rule: juhumaḥ before t becomes juhumas; tat before n becomes tan.

sandhi.type: visarga after a before a; the a kept
sandhi.rule: naḥ before a becomes no, and the initial a of astu is kept, not elided: see sandhi exceptions.

sandhi.type: visarga after a before a voiced consonant

sandhi_exceptions.note: naḥ astu is written no astu: the visarga becomes o, but the initial a is kept, where classical sandhi would elide it (no ’stu).

morphology.note: The preverb pari stands apart from its verb babhūva (tmesis), as often in the Veda: pari … babhūva, ‘has encompassed, has surpassed’.
Vedic neuter plural in -ā (viśvā for viśvāni), like tā for tāni in the same line.

translation.literal: O Prajāpati, no other than you has encompassed all these born things. With whatever desire we offer to you, let that be ours; may we be lords of riches.
translation.readable: Prajāpati, none but you holds all that has come to be. Whatever we desire as we make our offering to you, let it be ours; may we become masters of wealth.

anvaya: हे प्रजापते त्वत् अन्यः एतानि विश्वा जातानि ता न परि बभूव । यत्कामाः [वयम्] ते जुहुमः तत् नः अस्तु । वयम् रयीणाम् पतयः स्याम ।
syntax: A negative statement (na … anyaḥ … pari babhūva) with the ablative tvat governed by anyaḥ, and the object stated twice (etāni viśvā jātāni, resumed by tā). Then a relative clause whose subject is described by the bahuvrīhi yatkāmāḥ, resumed by tat in a third person imperative (astu), and a closing wish in the optative (syāma).

ambiguities.note: ‘Encompassed’ (held within) or ‘surpassed, overpowered’. The commentator takes bhū with pari as overpowering, «परिपूर्वो भवतिस्तिरस्कारार्थः», and explains it as creating, sustaining and withdrawing the worlds: none but Prajāpati does so.
The text says only Prajāpati. The commentator addresses him as Brahman and as the husband of Pārvatī, «हे प्रजापते ब्रह्मन्पार्वतीवल्लभ»; that identification is his.

metre.name: triṣṭubh
metre.note: As printed each half has 21 syllables: prajāpate na tvad etāny anyo (10) viśvā jātāni pari tā babhūva (11); yatkāmās te juhumas tan no astu (11) vayaṃ syāma patayo rayīṇām (10). Two pādas fall one short of eleven; reading tvad and syāma with two syllables each (tuvad, siyāma), as Vedic metre often requires, would make them regular, but the edition only reports the count.

beginner: This prayer is addressed to Prajāpati, the "lord of creatures", the creator. Its first half is a statement: no one other than you holds all that has been born. Its second half is a request: whatever we wish for when we make our offering to you, let it come to us, and may we become masters of wealth. The old commentator explains that only this lord creates, sustains and withdraws everything, and that the offering is made because of that. He adds that the same verse is used when water is offered at a meal given to brāhmaṇas. The verse is also known from the Ṛgveda. The edition reports what the words and the commentator say; it makes no claim about what making the offering brings.
analogy: Like a household acknowledging the one who keeps the whole estate before asking him for its share.

commentary.label: direct
commentary.text: It tells Prajāpati that no one other than he encompasses all created things, and asks that the object of the worshippers’ desire in offering to him be theirs, and that they become lords of riches.

commentary.q: How does the commentator read it?
commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: The anonymous commentator takes pari-bhū as overpowering, «परिपूर्वो भवतिस्तिरस्कारार्थः», and draws the sense: in creation, in sustaining and in withdrawal it is this lord alone who acts, «अपि तु सृष्टिकाले त्वमेव सृजसि जीवनकाले त्वमेव जीवयसि प्रलये त्वमेव त्वय्येवोपसंहरसि». The riches asked for are of two kinds, of learning and of enjoyment: «विद्याविनयसंपदामिहपरोपभोग्यभोगसंपदां च».

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Besides the offering into fire, the commentator names a second use: «अयमेव मन्त्रो ब्राह्मणभोजनादौ पार्वतीपतिप्रीतिकृदुदकदाने विनियुज्यते» — the same mantra is used when water is given at the start of a meal for brāhmaṇas, to please the lord of Pārvatī; then ‘we offer’ means offering food into the brāhmaṇa’s mouth as into fire.

schools.disagreement: No Vedānta-school commentary on this anuvāka is in the edition’s sources (Raṅgarāmānuja’s commentary on the Mahānārāyaṇa is not among them). The anonymous bhāṣya explains the words and the rite; it does not argue an Advaita, Viśiṣṭādvaita or Dvaita position here, so the edition gives none.

contemporary.text: The verse acknowledges before it asks: first that all that exists is held by another, then what the worshippers want. Acknowledging what one depends on before asking for more is a discipline in its own right. This is a modern reflection on the passage, not part of its traditional meaning.

reflect.beginner: What do you depend on that you rarely acknowledge?
reflect.deeper: The commentator reads ‘riches’ as both learning and enjoyment. Why might a prayer for wealth be read as including learning?
reflect.practice: Before asking anyone for something today, first say what you are grateful for in them.

references.text: No comment of Sāyaṇa’s or Bhaṭṭa Bhāskara’s on this anuvāka is in the edition’s sources: Sāyaṇa’s anuvākas 52–57 are missing from the digital text used here, and neither commentary file glosses these words; the edition’s concordance maps give no anuvāka of theirs for it. The anonymous bhāṣya is the only commentary quoted.
The verse is the last of the Ṛgveda’s hymn to Hiraṇyagarbha (Ṛgveda 10.121.10). The edition’s Ṛgveda source has only the first maṇḍala, so the parallel is noted here, not quoted.

flags.note: The Tirupati e-text alone reads यत्कमास्ते (short a), a witness error (corrections.json).
